body.en:
• A function packages a computation: function name($param, ...) { ... return $value; }. Call it by name with arguments: fare(265).
  • Parameters are the inputs at the doorway; arguments are the actual values handed in. return sends exactly one value back (return an array to smuggle out several).
  • PHP functions are global once defined - callable from anywhere below or above in the file - and names are case-insensitive (FARE() works, but use the declared spelling).
  • Discipline: a function computes; it does not echo banners. Output is the caller's choice - this keeps functions reusable across pages.
  • Vocabulary: define once, call many times. Total of messy copy-paste → one tested function.

h.en: Arguments: Defaults, Return Values, By Value vs By Reference

body.en:
• Default parameters: function fare($km, $rate = 1.2) - callers may skip trailing parameters; fare(265) uses the default rate, fare(265, 1.5) overrides it. Required parameters come first, optional ones last.
  • By value (default): PHP hands the function a copy - changing $n inside leaves the caller's variable untouched.
  • By reference: prefix & - function addTip(&$total) - and the function borrows the caller's actual variable; changes stick. Classic uses: swap($a,$b), accumulating into a result array.
  • Same trick inside the signature and at call time: sort($arr) is built-in by-reference - that is why it changes your array without returning it.
  • Rule of thumb: default to by-value; reach for & only when the function's job is to modify its argument.

h.en: Variable Scope: Local, Global and Static

body.en:
• Local scope: variables created inside a function live and die with the call - the outside world cannot see $tip, and the function cannot see your $total.
  • Global scope: script-level variables. Open the window deliberately with global $total; inside the function, or use the super-global array $GLOBALS['total'].
  • Static locals: static $calls = 0; survives between calls of the same function - a visit counter without globals.
  • Good style: pass inputs as parameters, return outputs - treat global as a last resort (hard to test, easy to tangle).

• Rounding family: round($x, 2), floor(), ceil() - money displays always round.
  • Magnitudes: abs(), max(...), min(...), pow($b, $e), sqrt(); integer division intdiv(17, 5) → 3.
  • Randomness: rand(1, 6) or random_int(1, 6) for cryptographic-quality picks (OTPs, dice).
  • Type shapers: (int)$s, (float)$s casts; checkers is_numeric() (true for "12.5") - Unit 3 uses these on every form field.
  • All and more live at php.net - knowing they exist beats memorising signatures.

• date("format") renders the current moment: d M Y → 29 Oct 2026; date("H:i") → 24h time. Format letters: d D m M y Y H h i s a l.
  • time() returns the Unix timestamp (seconds since 1970) - arithmetic-ready (time() + 86400 = tomorrow).
  • mktime(h, m, s, month, day, year) builds a timestamp; wrap in date() to read it.
  • strtotime("next Monday") parses English into a timestamp - surprisingly capable for booking deadlines.
  • Intervals and differences: date_create()/date_diff() or DateTime::diff give exact day gaps ("booked 12 days before travel").
  • Set the zone once for India: date_default_timezone_set("Asia/Kolkata").

• One ordered map type serves both habits. Indexed: numeric keys auto-assigned from 0 - $cities = ["Surat", "Vadodara"];, read with $cities[0].
  • Associative: named keys - $fare = ["SRT" => 250, "AMD" => 160];, read with $fare['SRT']. Keys are strings or ints; quotes only around strings.
  • Create empty $a = []; and append with $a[] = $v; (indexed) or $a['key'] = $v; (associative). Add, overwrite, delete with unset($a['key']).
  • Arrays are PHP's workhorse: form data ($_POST), database rows and config are all associative arrays.

• Arrays inside arrays: a list of students, each ["roll" => 7, "name" => "Asha", "marks" => [78, 81, 69]] - three dimensions deep.
  • Address precisely: $students[2]['marks'][1] reads row 2, sub-array, position 1.
  • Nested foreach walks the table naturally - an outer lap per record, an inner lap per field.
  • Mental image: rows of a spreadsheet stored in PHP memory; Unit 5 swaps this for real MySQL tables with the same shape.

• foreach ($a as $v) streams values; foreach ($a as $k => $v) streams keys too - the idiomatic PHP loop.
  • Common processing patterns: sum/count → average; max/min via comparisons; filter into a new array (only bookings above Rs 200); map (format every row as an HTML <li>).
  • The manual gearbox exists too: current(), next(), prev(), end(), reset() move an internal pointer - foreach resets and drives it for you.
  • Keep loops readable: give the value variable a real name ($booking, not $x).

• Measure: count($a); search: in_array($v, $a), array_search($v, $a) (returns key), array_key_exists().
  • Order: sort()/rsort() renumber keys (0..n) - fine for lists, fatal for assoc keys; use asort(), arsort() (by value) or ksort()/krsort() (by key) to keep pairs glued.
  • Combine and reshape: array_merge(), array_reverse(), array_slice(), array_unique().
  • Stack ends: array_push()/array_pop() (end), array_shift()/array_unshift() (front).
  • Bridges: implode(', ', $a) (array → string), explode(',', $s) (string → array), list($x, $y) = $pair unpacks; each() is long-deprecated - use foreach.

h.en: Quoting Styles: Single, Double, Heredoc, Nowdoc

body.en:
• Single quotes: literal text - '$fare' prints a dollar sign, not a value. Double quotes: interpolate variables - "Fare: $fare" expands in place.
  • Heredoc: echo <<<EOT ... EOT; - multi-line block that behaves like double quotes; perfect for HTML receipts with variables.
  • Nowdoc: <<<'EOT' (quoted marker) - multi-line AND literal; perfect for raw SQL or code samples.
  • Escapes inside double quotes: \n newline, \t tab, \$ literal dollar, \\ backslash.
  • Before echoing user data into HTML, escape with htmlspecialchars() - the first rule of safe output (Unit 3 drills it).

h.en: String Library Functions: Search, Replace, Compare (Practical 10)

body.en:
• Shape: strlen(), strtolower()/strtoupper(), ucfirst()/ucwords(), trim()/ltrim()/rtrim(), substr($s, 0, 3).
  • Find: strpos($hay, $needle) (0-based position or false), strrpos() (last), stristr()/strstr() (rest of string from match), case-insensitive twins carry the i.
  • Change: str_replace($find, $with, $s), substr_replace(), strrev(), str_repeat(), wordwrap().
  • Compare: strcmp()/strcasecmp() return negative/zero/positive - feed usort() callbacks.
  • Characters: chr(65) → "A", ord('A') → 65 for code-point tricks.
  • Trap: when a needle is NOT found, strpos returns false - but position 0 is also falsy, so always test with === false.

code.en:
<?php
// One tested function replaces copy-paste fare maths
function fare($km, $rate = 1.2, $minFare = 50) {
    $total = $km * $rate;
    return max($total, $minFare);   // never below the minimum fare
}

function receipt($city, $km, $rate = 1.2) {
    $f = fare($km, $rate);
    return "$city: {$km} km, Rs $f";
}

echo receipt("Bharuch", 60), "\n";      // uses default rate
echo receipt("Ahmedabad", 265), "\n";
echo receipt("Gandhinagar", 265, 1.5), "\n";  // override rate
echo receipt("Navsari", 30), "\n";      // min fare kicks in
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
Bharuch: 60 km, Rs 72
Ahmedabad: 265 km, Rs 318
Gandhinagar: 265 km, Rs 397.5
Navsari: 30 km, Rs 50

expl.en: fare() has one required parameter ($km) and two with defaults - skip them and the defaults apply. return hands one value back; receipt() shows function-calling-function composition. Note {$km} braced interpolation inside the double-quoted string.

title.en: Passing by value vs by reference (swap demo)

code.en:
<?php
function trySwap($a, $b) {          // BY VALUE: gets copies
    $t = $a; $a = $b; $b = $t;
}
function swap(&$a, &$b) {           // BY REFERENCE: gets originals
    $t = $a; $a = $b; $b = $t;
}

$x = "Surat"; $y = "Mumbai";
trySwap($x, $y);
echo "after trySwap: $x / $y\n";    // unchanged!

swap($x, $y);
echo "after swap&  : $x / $y\n";    // swapped for real

// practical use: accumulate INTO a caller's array
function addBooking(&$list, $seat) {
    $list[] = $seat;                // appends to caller's array
}
$bookings = ["12A"];
addBooking($bookings, "14C");
addBooking($bookings, "3B");
echo "bookings: ", implode(", ", $bookings), "\n";
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
after trySwap: Surat / Mumbai
after swap&  : Mumbai / Surat
bookings: 12A, 14C, 3B

expl.en: trySwap shuffles photocopies - the caller's variables survive untouched. With &$a, &$b the function borrows the originals and the swap is real. The addBooking pattern (array passed by reference) is how helper functions grow a caller's data.

code.en:
<?php
$total = 100;                       // GLOBAL scope variable

function addTip($tip) {
    global $total;                  // open the window
    $total += $tip;
    $localNote = "added $tip";      // LOCAL: dies with the call
    echo "  inside: $localNote\n";
}

function visitCounter() {
    static $visits = 0;             // STATIC: survives between calls
    $visits++;
    return $visits;
}

addTip(15);
addTip(10);
echo "global total now: $total\n";

echo "via \$GLOBALS: ", $GLOBALS["total"], "\n";

echo "visits: ", visitCounter(), ", ", visitCounter(), ", ", visitCounter(), "\n";
// echo $localNote;  // would be empty - local scope!
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
  inside: added 15
  inside: added 10
global total now: 125
via $GLOBALS: 125
visits: 1, 2, 3

expl.en: Three scopes in one program: $localNote vanishes when addTip ends; global $total (or $GLOBALS['total']) lets a function modify a script-level variable; static $visits is a local that remembers across calls - perfect for counters.

code.en:
<?php
$bill = 102.789;
echo "round : ", round($bill), " / ", round($bill, 2), "\n";
echo "floor : ", floor($bill), "  ceil: ", ceil($bill), "\n";
echo "abs   : ", abs(-42), "\n";
echo "max   : ", max(250, 160, 320), "  min: ", min(250, 160, 320), "\n";
echo "pow   : ", pow(2, 10), "  sqrt: ", sqrt(144), "\n";
echo "intdiv: ", intdiv(17, 5), "  mod: ", 17 % 5, "\n";

echo "dice  : ", rand(1, 6), "  otp : ", random_int(1000, 9999), "\n";

// is_numeric checks form strings before calculating
$raw = "12.5";                      // as it would arrive from a form
echo "is_numeric('12.5'): ", var_export(is_numeric($raw), true), "\n";
if (is_numeric($raw)) {
    echo "per km for 40 km: Rs ", (float)$raw * 40, "\n";
}
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
round : 103 / 102.79
floor : 102  ceil: 103
abs   : 42
max   : 320  min: 160
pow   : 1024  sqrt: 12
intdiv: 3  mod: 2
dice  : 5  otp : 2100
is_numeric('12.5'): true
per km for 40 km: Rs 500

expl.en: PHP's math library covers rounding (round/floor/ceil), magnitudes (abs/max/min/pow/sqrt), integer division (intdiv) and randomness (rand, random_int for OTPs). is_numeric validates string input before you trust it in arithmetic - the Unit 3 habit.

code.en:
<?php
date_default_timezone_set("Asia/Kolkata");

echo "Today       : ", date("d M Y"), "\n";
echo "Full banner : ", date("l, jS F Y"), "\n";
echo "Time        : ", date("h:i A"), "\n";
echo "Timestamp   : ", time(), " seconds since 1970\n";

$travel = mktime(6, 30, 0, 11, 15, 2026);   // bus departs 15 Nov 06:30
echo "Travel day  : ", date("d M Y h:i A", $travel), "\n";

$days = (int)(($travel - time()) / 86400);
echo "Days to trip: $days\n";

echo "Next Monday : ", date("d M", strtotime("next Monday")), "\n";
echo "Deadline    : ", date("d M Y", strtotime("+7 days")), "\n";

// date_diff for exact gaps
$booked = date_create("2026-10-01");
$trip   = date_create("2026-10-29");
$gap    = date_diff($booked, $trip);
echo "Booked ", $gap->days, " days before travel\n";
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
Today       : 29 Oct 2026
Full banner : Thursday, 29th October 2026
Time        : 01:05 AM
Timestamp   : 1793216144 seconds since 1970
Travel day  : 15 Nov 2026 06:30 AM
Days to trip: 17
Next Monday : 02 Nov
Deadline    : 05 Nov 2026
Booked 28 days before travel

expl.en: date() renders any timestamp with format letters; time() is seconds-since-1970 (so +86400 = tomorrow); mktime() builds timestamps, strtotime() parses English ("next Monday"), and date_diff() measures exact gaps between two dates - the booking-window calculation every ticket site needs.

code.en:
<?php
// INDEXED array: positions 0, 1, 2 ...
$cities = ["Surat", "Bharuch", "Vadodara"];
$cities[] = "Ahmedabad";            // append
echo "First stop: $cities[0]\n";
echo "Stops: ", count($cities), "\n";
foreach ($cities as $c) echo "  -> $c\n";

// ASSOCIATIVE array: named keys
$fare = ["SRT" => 250, "BRC" => 120, "AMD" => 160];
$fare["GANDHI"] = 300;              // add by key
$fare["SRT"] = 260;                 // overwrite
echo "Fare to AMD: Rs ", $fare["AMD"], "\n";
foreach ($fare as $code => $amt) {
    echo "  $code : Rs $amt\n";
}
unset($fare["BRC"]);                // delete a pair
echo "after unset: ", implode(", ", array_keys($fare)), "\n";
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
First stop: Surat
Stops: 4
  -> Surat
  -> Bharuch
  -> Vadodara
  -> Ahmedabad
Fare to AMD: Rs 160
  SRT : Rs 260
  BRC : Rs 120
  AMD : Rs 160
  GANDHI : Rs 300
after unset: SRT, AMD, GANDHI

expl.en: Indexed arrays order items by position (auto keys from 0, append with $a[]); associative arrays pair named keys with values ($fare['SRT']). Add/overwrite by assigning a key, delete with unset, walk either with foreach - with $k => $v when keys matter.

code.en:
<?php
$students = [
    ["roll" => 7,  "name" => "Asha",  "marks" => ["SE" => 78, "Java" => 81, "IWD" => 69]],
    ["roll" => 12, "name" => "Bhuvi", "marks" => ["SE" => 91, "Java" => 66, "IWD" => 72]],
    ["roll" => 19, "name" => "Chirag","marks" => ["SE" => 55, "Java" => 74, "IWD" => 88]],
];

echo "Row 2 name      : ", $students[1]["name"], "\n";
echo "Row 3 IWD marks : ", $students[2]["marks"]["IWD"], "\n\n";

// nested foreach: whole table, with totals
foreach ($students as $s) {
    $sum = 0;
    foreach ($s["marks"] as $sub => $m) $sum += $m;
    printf("%-8s (roll %2d): total %d / 270\n", $s["name"], $s["roll"], $sum);
}
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
Row 2 name      : Bhuvi
Row 3 IWD marks : 88

Asha     (roll  7): total 228 / 270
Bhuvi    (roll 12): total 229 / 270
Chirag   (roll 19): total 217 / 270

expl.en: Arrays inside arrays model a spreadsheet: each student is an associative record, marks is itself an associative array. Address with chained brackets ($students[2]['marks']['IWD']) and walk with nested foreach - outer lap per student, inner lap per subject. printf keeps columns neat.

code.en:
<?php
$shopping = ["milk" => 62, "bread" => 45, "eggs" => 78, "tea" => 140];

echo "count     : ", count($shopping), "\n";
echo "in_array  : ", var_export(in_array(78, $shopping), true), "\n";
echo "key exists: ", var_export(array_key_exists("bread", $shopping), true), "\n";

// sort WITHOUT breaking name <-> price pairs
$cheap = $shopping;
asort($cheap);
echo "cheapest first -> ", implode(", ", array_map(fn($k,$v)=>"$k:$v", array_keys($cheap), $cheap)), "\n";

$list = ["Surat", "Vadodara", "Ahmedabad"];
sort($list);                        // renumbers keys 0..n - fine here
echo "sorted list : ", implode(", ", $list), "\n";

$merged = array_merge(["jam" => 95], $shopping);
echo "merged keys : ", implode(", ", array_keys($merged)), "\n";
echo "reversed    : ", implode(", ", array_reverse($list)), "\n";

array_push($list, "Gandhinagar");
echo "pushed/popped: ", array_pop($list), " popped; now ", count($list), "\n";

// list() unpacks slots; explode/implode bridge strings
list($a, $b, $c) = ["red", "green", "blue"];
echo "list() : $a | $b | $c\n";
echo "explode: ", count(explode(",", "12A,14C,3B")), " seat codes\n";
?>

programs.out:
$ php index.php
count     : 4
in_array  : true
key exists: true
cheapest first -> bread:45, milk:62, eggs:78, tea:140
sorted list : Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara
merged keys : jam, milk, bread, eggs, tea
reversed    : Vadodara, Surat, Ahmedabad
pushed/popped: Gandhinagar popped; now 3
list() : red | green | blue
explode: 3 seat codes

expl.en: Highlights: asort sorts by value keeping keys glued (sort renumbers and destroys names); array_merge glues arrays; array_push/pop treat the end like a stack; list() unpacks a small array into variables; explode/implode convert CSV text to arrays and back.

<?php
$name = "  Surat Express  ";
echo "strlen : ", strlen($name), "\n";                 // includes spaces!
echo "trim   : '", trim($name), "'\n";

$s = "Surat to Ahmedabad";

$pos = strpos($s, "to");

echo "miss   : ", var_export(strpos($s, "zzz"),

if (strpos($s, "Surat") === false) { echo "not found\n"; } else { echo "Surat found\n"; }
echo "stristr: ", stristr($s, "TO"), "\n";             // case-insensitive, rest-of-string

echo "replace: ", str_replace("to", "-", $s), "\n";
echo "strrev : ", strrev("madam"), "\n";
echo "repeat : ", str_repeat("-", 20), "\n";

case   : SURAT EXPRESS -> Surat Express
substr : Surat / Ahmedabad
strpos : 6
miss   : false  (== false would misfire on position 0)
Surat found

expl.en: The string toolkit: measure (strlen), clean (trim, case fixers), slice (substr, negative length reads from the end), locate (strpos 0-based or false; stristr case-insensitive), mutate (str_replace, strrev, str_repeat), compare (strcmp/strcasecmp) and hop between characters and codes (chr/ord). Golden rule: test strpos(...) === false - never == false.

q.en: How do you define and call a PHP function?

a.en: function fare($km) { ... return $v; } defines it globally; call by name with arguments: fare(265).

q.en: Parameters vs arguments?

a.en: Parameters are the placeholders in the definition ($km); arguments are the actual values at the call (265).

q.en: What does return do?

a.en: Hands exactly one value back to the caller and ends the function; return an array when you need several results.

q.en: What are default (optional) parameters?

a.en: Parameters with preset values - function f($km, $rate = 1.2); callers may omit them; required params come first.

q.en: Passing by value vs by reference?

a.en: By value passes a copy (default - caller's variable is safe); &$n passes the original, so the function can modify it (swap, accumulate).

q.en: Why does sort($a) change the array without returning?

a.en: sort is a built-in pass-by-reference function - it edits the caller's array directly.

q.en: What is variable scope?

a.en: Where a variable is visible: function locals die with the call; script-level globals sit outside; neither sees the other by default.

q.en: How do you access a global inside a function?

a.en: Declare global $total; at the top of the function, or use $GLOBALS['total'] - the super-global array.

q.en: What is a static local variable?

a.en: static $c = 0; inside a function keeps its value between calls - a private counter.

q.en: Why prefer parameters over global?

a.en: Globals tangle dependencies and are hard to test; parameters + return keep functions self-contained and reusable.

q.en: Name six mathematical built-ins.

a.en: round, floor, ceil, abs, max/min, pow, sqrt, intdiv, rand/random_int.

q.en: round vs floor vs ceil?

a.en: round() nearest (optional decimals); floor() always down; ceil() always up - money displays use round($x, 2).

q.en: rand() vs random_int()?

a.en: Both pick integers in a range; random_int is cryptographically secure - use it for OTPs and anything security-related.

q.en: What does is_numeric("12.5") return?

a.en: true - it validates numeric-looking strings before you calculate with form input.

q.en: What does date('d M Y') produce?

a.en: e.g. 29 Oct 2026 - date() renders a timestamp using format letters (default: right now).

q.en: What is a Unix timestamp?

a.en: Seconds elapsed since 1 Jan 1970 (UTC); time() returns it - arithmetic-ready, e.g. +86400 is tomorrow.

q.en: mktime vs strtotime?

a.en: mktime(h,m,s,mon,day,year) builds a timestamp from parts; strtotime('next Monday') parses English text into a timestamp.

q.en: How do you compute days between two dates?

a.en: date_diff(date_create($a), date_create($b))->days - or subtract timestamps and divide by 86400.

q.en: Why set date_default_timezone_set?

a.en: So date/time functions speak local time - Asia/Kolkata for Indian projects; otherwise they use UTC.

q.en: What are the two indexing habits of PHP arrays?

a.en: Indexed arrays have numeric keys from 0; associative arrays map named keys to values - one ordered-map type serves both.

q.en: How do you append to an array?

a.en: $a[] = $v; for the next numeric slot, or $a['key'] = $v; under a named key; unset($a['key']) deletes.

q.en: Read $students[2]['marks'][1]?

a.en: Third element (index 2), its 'marks' sub-array, element 1 - chained brackets descend dimensions.

q.en: Give a real use of a multidimensional array.

a.en: A students table: each element is a record [roll, name, marks[subject=>score]] - a spreadsheet in memory.

q.en: Two forms of foreach?

a.en: foreach ($a as $v) for values; foreach ($a as $k => $v) when keys matter - it resets the array pointer automatically.

q.en: What do current(), next(), end() do?

a.en: They walk the array's internal pointer manually - foreach drives this pointer for you.

q.en: sort vs asort - the danger?

a.en: sort renumbers keys 0..n, destroying assoc key names; asort sorts by value keeping key-value pairs intact (ksort by key).

q.en: in_array vs array_key_exists?

a.en: in_array($v,$a) searches VALUES; array_key_exists('k',$a) searches KEYS; array_search returns the matching key.

q.en: array_push/array_pop do what?

a.en: Add/remove at the END - stack behaviour; array_shift/unshift work the front.

q.en: implode and explode?

a.en: implode(',', $a) joins an array into a string; explode(',', $s) splits a string into an array - the CSV bridge.

q.en: What does list() do?

a.en: Unpacks array slots into named variables: list($r, $g, $b) = [255, 128, 0];

q.en: Difference between single and double quotes?

a.en: Single quotes are literal ('$x' prints $x); double quotes interpolate variables ("$x" expands). Which escapes work? \n \t \$ only in double quotes/heredoc.

q.en: What is heredoc?

a.en: <<<EOT ... EOT; - a multi-line string that expands variables, like double quotes without quote juggling.

q.en: What is nowdoc?

a.en: <<<'EOT' ... EOT; - heredoc's literal twin: multi-line, no interpolation; ideal for raw code/SQL text.

q.en: Why htmlspecialchars() before echoing user text?

a.en: It neutralises < > & " ' into entities so user input cannot inject HTML/JS into your pages.

q.en: strlen/substr examples?

a.en: strlen('Surat') = 5; substr('Surat', 0, 3) = 'Sur'; substr('Surat', -3) = 'rat' (negative = from the end).

q.en: strpos gotcha?

a.en: Returns 0-based position OR false; position 0 is falsy, so test === false or you misread a match at the start.

q.en: strstr vs stristr?

a.en: Both return the haystack from the first needle onward; stristr ignores case. strpos only returns a position.

q.en: strcmp return values?

a.en: Negative / zero / positive for less / equal / greater - feeds usort comparison callbacks; strcasecmp ignores case.

q.en: chr and ord?

a.en: chr(65) -> 'A'; ord('A') -> 65 - convert between characters and ASCII/byte codes.

q.en: Which Unit 2 functions would power a grade sheet?

a.en: A marks array per student, foreach totals, max/min, asort for rank order, and a function returning the grade ladder from Unit 1.
